thread:
Alex R: seeing a spike in 5xx from the hosted API since ~10:05 UTC, p99 latency rising too. Pager firing.
Maya S: on it, grabbing metrics. any customer-facing errors? :rotating_light:
Alex R: errors look like downstream kv-cache timeouts, a bunch of requests hitting model pool which then OOMs. early signs of kv-cache thrash. link to charts: https://dash.redwood-infra/requests/hosted-api/5xx
incident-bot: [INCIDENT] Pager triggered: /services/hosted-api/importance=high — 42 alerts in last 5m (see runbook suggestions)
Lin T: I can take primary now. Alex, do you want to stay as secondary?
Alex R: yes. Lin primary, Maya secondary. I'll stay nearby for handoff notes.
Maya S: quick customer triage — looks like high error rate concentrated on model 'redwood/gpt-neo-small' variant used by ACME-Pay integrations. ACME has ~18% of errors. tagging customers: @acme-pay ops.
Lin T: following the kv-cache runbook first: https://runbooks.redwood/kv-cache-thrash — steps 1-3 to probe and isolate. I'm starting a read-only cache bypass for the affected pools.
Alex R: good. If we bypass cache, expect increase in GPU throughput — have autoscale ready. Maya, can you open a quick scale on the dedicated pool?
Maya S: scaling dedicated/gpu-pool-2 +2 nodes now via infra-console: https://console.redwood/infrastructure/pools/gpu-pool-2 — command: ```infractl scale pool gpu-pool-2 --count +2```
PagerDuty: Route changed: escalation -> Lin T (primary) -> Maya S (secondary).
Lin T: cache bypass applied to route /v1/generate for model redwood/gpt-neo-small. Monitoring 1m windows.
Alex R: I'm toggling fallback policy to model variant 'gpt-neo-small-quant' to reduce memory pressure if OOM persists. config: ```routing.fallback=model:gpt-neo-small-quant,threshold=0.15```
Maya S: +2 nodes up, healthchecks passing. Token throughput increased, tail latency still elevated but 5xx trending down from 18%->6% in the last 3m.
Lin T: adding KV diagnostic logs to the incident thread: ```kubectl logs -l app=kv-cache -n infra | grep stall | tail -n 200``` — seeing repeated sync stalls at 10:04 UTC.
Alex R: note for handoff: suspected root cause = cache eviction storm caused by unusual token-length distribution from a specific client pattern -> downstream KV saturates -> model pool memory pressure -> OOMs. Mitigations applied: cache bypass, pool scale, fallback model.
Maya S: customer comms draft: "We detected elevated errors affecting a subset of Gen endpoints; mitigation applied and we are monitoring. Follow-up with root cause and ETA for permanent fix." Shall I send to CSM?
Lin T: yes, go ahead. Also creating tracking ticket: RDW-INC-2026 (linked to runbooks) with next steps: permanent cache guardrail, improved model fallback thresholds, additional alerts on cache eviction rate.
incident-bot: Incident timeline updated. Current status: mitigations in place, monitoring. Severity: elevated -> operational.
Alex R: OK team — I'm writing brief handoff for the next shift: primary = Lin T, secondary = Maya S, notes: continue monitoring 5xx for next 2 hours, watch GPU memory S0/S1, rollback cache bypass only after sustained p50/p95 normal. Open follow-up RFC for cache guardrails.
Maya S: acknowledged. I'll keep watch and let oncall know if error rate > 5% for 5m. Leaving a bookmark to runbooks: model fallback doc https://runbooks.redwood/model-fallbacks and routing policy cheatsheet https://runbooks.redwood/routing/policy-quickrefs
Lin T: logging a short checklist for handover: 1) confirm 5xx < 2% over 10m, 2) confirm dedicated pool stable, 3) confirm no single-customer spike, 4) snapshot logs -> upload to RDW-INC-2026.
Alex R: thanks — I'll be on-call for another 30m. If it reverts, escalate page to infra-sre.
Maya S: thanks everyone. Leaving brief note in shift doc: https://confluence.redwood/oncall/weekend-notes#5009876543
PagerDuty: Incident acknowledged by Lin T.
Lin T: signing off active mitigation in 25m if metrics hold. Handoff ready for next primary (Nadia or Priya).
Alex R: exact handoff summary will be appended to RDW-INC-2026 before I step away.
Maya S: copy. good job team :thumbsup:
